registers.name: CONTROL_MODE
registers.description: Firmware-selected control mode and sequencing policy control. This register is reachable through the declared CSR/MMIO decode path.

fields.name: control_mode
fields.description: Control mode encoding. Implemented values are design-defined and used by the actuator validator.

fields.name: seq_depth_mode
fields.description: Sequencing depth enable. 0 selects single-outstanding behavior; 1 enables bounded depth-2 policy when supported.

registers.name: TIMEOUT_FRESHNESS
registers.description: Programmable timeout and freshness thresholds used by the streaming controller.

fields.name: timeout_threshold
fields.description: Maximum age in cycles before timeout handling asserts.

fields.name: freshness_threshold
fields.description: Maximum allowed freshness delta for request/response validation.

registers.name: CLAMP_LIMITS
registers.description: Actuator clamp bounds used by the actuator validator.

registers.name: STATUS_FAULT_CLEAR
registers.description: Status and sticky fault clear register. Write-one-to-clear semantics apply to sticky fault bits; writing zero leaves bits unchanged.

fields.name: sticky_timeout
fields.description: Sticky timeout fault. Set by timeout detection; clear with write-one-to-clear.

fields.name: sticky_stale
fields.description: Sticky stale-data fault. Set by freshness expiry; clear with write-one-to-clear.

fields.name: sticky_invalid_packet
fields.description: Sticky invalid-packet fault. Set by malformed packet or header rejection; clear with write-one-to-clear.

fields.name: sticky_clamp_violation
fields.description: Sticky clamp-violation fault. Set when intent exceeds configured limits; clear with write-one-to-clear.

fields.name: fault_latch_clear
fields.description: Write-one-to-clear strobe bits for the sticky fault fields. Clearing does not re-enable actuator validity by itself.

registers.name: SEQUENCE_COUNTERS
registers.description: Sequencing status counters exposed for firmware observability.

fields.name: outstanding_sequence_counter
fields.description: Current outstanding transaction count, bounded by the configured depth policy.

sources.name: sticky_timeout
sources.description: Sticky timeout fault status available to software handling. No dedicated interrupt pin is defined in the spec; this source represents software-visible fault status.

sources.name: sticky_stale
sources.description: Sticky stale-data fault status available to software handling.

sources.name: sticky_invalid_packet
sources.description: Sticky invalid-packet fault status available to software handling.

sources.name: sticky_clamp_violation
sources.description: Sticky clamp-violation fault status available to software handling.

init_sequence: Assert reset and wait for synchronous release.
Program CONTROL_MODE at 0x00 with control_mode and seq_depth_mode.
Program TIMEOUT_FRESHNESS at 0x08 with timeout_threshold and freshness_threshold.
Program CLAMP_LIMITS at 0x10 with clamp_min and clamp_max.
Read VERSION_CAPABILITY at 0x28 to confirm version/capability identity.
Clear any pre-existing sticky faults by writing ones to the selected bits in STATUS_FAULT_CLEAR at 0x18.
polling_sequence: Poll SEQUENCE_COUNTERS at 0x20 to observe accepted and outstanding sequence state.
Poll STATUS_FAULT_CLEAR at 0x18 to read sticky fault bits and confirm whether command validity is inhibited.

Poll transport/status outputs for status_mode, status_outstanding_tid, status_age_counter, status_timeout, status_stale, status_invalid, status_fallback_active, and status_clamp_active as part of normal supervision.
irq_sequence: On any sticky fault indication, halt issuance of new commands until software has inspected status, cleared the relevant sticky bits in 0x18, and revalidated configuration.
After clearing, verify that the next transaction is valid before expecting act_cmd_valid to assert again.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The register map uses the declared 64-bit CSR/MMIO window and is reachable through RTL decode.
No incompatible hierarchy, ports, or bus protocol have been introduced.
No substitute or fallback command is defined; unsafe conditions must inhibit actuator validity rather than replace the requested command.
